set.approach: Park beside the Southfork road where the Dental Floss drainage meets it, a little west of the Legg Creek drainage. Cross the valley floor to the mouth of the straight, obvious drainage and put crampons on there. The ice climbs the main drainage in bulges and curtains with a lot of walking between flows.

review.notes: Parking and location from the route page; crossing the valley floor and crampons from the Witched Woman page. No source states a descent.

set.approach: Park near the Valley Ranch mailbox and walk up the Triptych drainage, which cuts into the hillside north of the road. Just past the Hostile Takeover flow, look to the right for a thin chimney. The ledge above that chimney is the base of the route.

review.notes: Chimney and ledge from the route page; Triptych drainage and ranch mailbox parking from the Hostile Takeover and Triptych Pillars pages. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park off the road near the Valley Ranch mailbox and head into the Triptych drainage on the north hillside. The flow is on the left side of that drainage.
set.descent_text: The route can be rappelled from bolts at the top. A walk-off to the east also exists, but the rappel is the quicker way down.

review.notes: Everything from the route page except the mailbox parking, which the Triptych Pillars page also gives.

set.approach: Enter the Triptych drainage on the north hillside and go toward the Hostile Takeover flow. Climb or walk around the first ice step, which is a modest height, then look to the right for the icy chimney.
set.descent_text: The route is rappelled from V-threads.

review.notes: Approach and V-thread rappels from the route page; Triptych drainage corroborated by neighbours.

set.approach: Walk up the Dental Floss drainage, crossing many small steps and stretches of low-angle ice. The flow pours into the drainage from the left, directly above. The main Dental Floss ice cuts right toward the chimney pitch, so stay left for this one.

review.notes: Approach from the route page; Witched Woman page places it on the left of the drainage. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park just past the ranch road that branches left near the Valley Ranch mailbox, then cross the sagebrush toward the pillars, which show high on the north hillside. Drop into the drainage where it leaves the hill. The creek bed is often icy with loose rock, and a bulge or curtain of ice breaks it every so often. The drainage can look like a dead-end canyon, but a hidden exit on the right appears only once you are directly beneath it. Thin ice may cross a small cliff band near the amphitheater, which can be bypassed on either side.
set.descent_text: Walk above the pillars first to look over the options. The way down mixes rappelling with downclimbing, and a tree above the middle pillar often carries slings. Much of the ice is too low-angle to rappel and too steep to walk, so downclimbing eats up most of the time.

review.notes: Single detailed route page; mailbox parking agrees with the Hostile Takeover page.

set.approach: Park along the road and cross the valley to the mouth of the Dental Floss drainage, where crampons go on. Follow the main drainage up past Too Much Goose, which appears on the left if it has formed, to a deep chimney. The route is on the left wall of the chimney just before it narrows.

review.notes: Single detailed route page; Too Much Goose page agrees on the left-hand side of the drainage. No descent stated.

set.approach: The route follows the large, obvious drainage on the north side of the road, which looks almost like a canyon. Park by the cottonwood trees where the first two pitches can be seen from the road. The approach is among the shorter ones in the valley, and short WI3 steps with brief walks between them lead to the main pitches.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling the route, mostly from V-threads and bolted stations on the climber's left of the steep pitches below the fifth, with trees serving for a few of the pitches. A walk-off is possible from a point below the fifth-pitch amphitheater.

review.notes: Parking, route line and descent from the route page; area page agrees on the drainage.

set.approach: The route is the left-hand line in the bowl that holds the fifth pitch of Broken Hearts. Reach the bowl by climbing the lower pitches of Broken Hearts, which follow the large drainage on the north side of the road.

review.notes: Location in the bowl from two pages; approach by the lower pitches from the route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Deer Creek trailhead, hike the trail past three sets of switchbacks and cross the large creek that drains Slogger. A short climb of switchbacks leads past the clearing, a wide clearing on a steep scree slope. A little farther, the drainage appears on the right (north). Walk the rolling ice in the creek bed a short way to the first pitch. Smooth Emerald Milkshake uses the same approach.
set.descent_text: Slings are in place on trees to the left of the first pitch, near the base of the amphitheater, and atop the pillar on its right side, giving rappel anchors down the route.

review.notes: Single detailed route page; Smooth Emerald Milkshake confirms shared approach.

set.approach: Follow the Deer Creek trail. Bitches Brew and Transient Alterations lie on the right, Smooth Emerald Milkshake on the left, and this route is in the drainage just left of Smooth Emerald Milkshake. Leave the trail by dropping down a steep slope, find a way across the river, and walk upstream a short distance to the base.

review.notes: Single route page; neighbour page places it across the way from Transient Alterations.

set.approach: Start from the Deer Creek trailhead and follow the Bitches Brew approach as far as its drainage. Walk and climb down that drainage to the bed of Deer Creek, which may need a downclimb of a fixed rope or a rappel if the rope is gone, then go a short way upstream to the base, where the ice pours straight into the creek. This route lies in avalanche terrain. Check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Rappel and downclimb the route; carry webbing for building anchors. The usual descent starts from the top of the rock band, where the drainage splits above the ice.

review.notes: Single detailed route page, with avalanche warning; Bitches Brew page confirms the shared approach.

set.approach: Start at the Deer Creek trailhead, the last one before the campground, and follow the trail to a major drainage crossing, where Slogger shows just below. After the trail switchbacks up a little, the Ghosts come into view across the creek. Shortly before the clearing, drop down a steep gully to the creek and follow it downstream to the base. Do not go farther down the creek, where drop-offs and unfrozen pools are common.

review.notes: Single route page; the clearing and Slogger crossing agree with the Bitches Brew page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park in the large lot on the right side of the road, just before the Deer Creek bridge, and hike straight up the creek to a deep chimney on the right.

review.notes: Parking and creek hike from the route page; area page confirms the Deer Creek trailhead. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Deer Creek trailhead, climb the sandy switchbacks until the trail traverses above the creek, then through another short set of switchbacks. Past them the ice shows above the trail. Step off the trail onto the first broad flat after that second switchback set and work up the drainage to the ice.

review.notes: Single route page; area page confirms trailhead. No descent stated.

set.approach: The flow pours off a cliff band north of the road, a short way upstream from Deer Creek campground. Hike straight up the ridge on the east side of the route's drainage; it is steep, with a lot of elevation to gain for a short pitch.
set.descent_text: A V-thread can be built near the top of the flow for rappelling or lowering.

review.notes: Single route page; area page confirms the campground setting.

set.approach: Go up the gully just left of The Main Vein. The approach is unpleasant, with a long scree slog in its final stretch.
set.descent_text: Cross to skier's right and work down past the foot of the route to a scree field that lets you boot down.

review.notes: Single route page; Main Vein page confirms the neighbouring line.

set.approach: Park between the campground and the road's end, a bit west of the campground, then head due north to the foot of the route. The upper pitches can be seen from the road, which helps with choosing a parking spot.

review.notes: Single route page; the area page confirms its place near the campground. No route-wide descent stated.

set.descent_text: Rappel from a V-thread, or from trees on the left.

review.notes: Single route page; no approach stated.

set.approach: Hike up Cabin Creek and turn up a drainage on the right, which drops all the way to the river. Depending on conditions you may walk ice up to the base, or dry-climb a small gash on the right.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. The first pitch has right-hand bolts at its top for the anchor, and the upper pitches have anchors above them.

review.notes: Route page; Wyoming Wave page confirms anchors above its pitches, which are the upper part of this route.

set.approach: Leave the car where the South Fork road ends by Cabin Creek and hike north and west to the creek. Follow the creek up the drainage to the first pitch of ice.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. The first step can be avoided by walking around it on the climber's right, close to the big rappel tree.

review.notes: Single route page; area page confirms Cabin Creek at the end of the road.

set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling from a natural thread anchor.

review.notes: Single route page; located beside the third pitch of Chasing the Sun. No approach stated.

set.approach: Hike up Cabin Creek, passing the drainage that leads to Cabin Fever. Pass up a small flow that has a big pool under it and keep walking; the route is on the left. The approach can cross avalanche debris. Check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Single route page; Cabin Fever page confirms the neighbouring drainage. No descent stated.

set.approach: Climb Cabin Fever, then walk up the creek a few minutes. The obvious flow on the left is this route.
set.descent_text: Good rappel anchors sit above each pitch, so the route is rappelled.

review.notes: Single route page; Cabin Fever page confirms the shared drainage.

set.approach: Park at the Barronette Peak pullout on Highway 212 and walk down the road to the seventh creek drainage. Follow the creek until it narrows, then traverse diagonally up through trees toward the south, staying above the next gully system, to reach the base of the falls. Most Abiathar ice lies in avalanche-prone gullies; this line is the exception, in a safer spot. Check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page for the walk-in; area page for the avalanche context and the pullout. No descent stated.

set.approach: Use the third and fourth creek drainages on the northwest face. Follow the creek to a rocky outcrop with a wide rib coming down on the right, climb the rib until just below a cliff, then traverse left through a shallow gully into the main gully. Go by a short ice step on your left and continue up the left side of the drainage. These gullies are avalanche terrain. Check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Rappel from a mix of thread anchors and trees on the climber's left.

review.notes: Single route page; area page confirms the drainages and the avalanche exposure.

set.descent_text: The route can be rappelled. Be careful at the top rappel, as the anchor above the ice is only just within reach.

review.notes: Single route page; area page confirms the route's sector. No approach given for the winter line.

set.approach: In winter the Teton Canyon road is closed to vehicles, so ski or snowmobile up it to the scout camp. Walk past the Boy Scout camp and pick a line through the trees to the cliff. The falls show from the road along the camp's side.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the tree on the right at the top, using a V-thread where needed.

review.notes: Route page; Teton Canyon page for winter road closure and approach by ski.

set.approach: In winter the Teton Canyon road is closed to vehicles, so ski or snowmobile up it. Cross Teton Creek on the Boy Scout camp bridge and go up the drainage into the cirque. The ice pillar hangs at the back of the cirque and can be spotted from the road or the ski track just west of the bridge.

review.notes: Icefall visibility from the route page; bridge and drainage from the area and mixed-list pages.
